rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't render configuration, annotations or a mode for ingress-nginx or any other retired or archived ingress controller, and have `values.schema.json` reject such a controller value.
rules.why: ingress-nginx is retired and archived and gets no security fixes, so a chart that configures it points operators at unpatched software.
rules.check: Look for `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/*` annotations, an `nginx` option for an ingress controller value, or a schema enum that allows it.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't give an enabled Ingress a default ingress controller. Make the operator name it explicitly, and fail rendering through the schema or `fail` when it is missing.
rules.why: If the chart guesses the controller, it renders the wrong backend TLS, and the release then serves a failing or unverified hop with no warning.
rules.check: Look for a default value for the ingress controller in values.yaml, or templates that fall back to one controller's annotations when none is set.

rules.statement: Never give an ingress controller, Gateway or router a Secret that holds the pods' serving private key to verify backend TLS. Verify against an object that holds only the CA (for example a ConfigMap with just `ca.crt`), or against the controller's own Secret.
rules.why: A router needs only the CA and its own client certificate, never a pod's private key. `BackendTLSPolicy` also can't read Secrets.
rules.check: Check that `BackendTLSPolicy` caCertificateRefs, Traefik `ServersTransport` rootCAs/certificatesSecrets, and similar backend-TLS references point at a CA-only object or the ingress Secret, not at the pods' serving certificate Secret.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't use `lookup` to build or populate resources.
rules.why: `lookup` returns nothing under `helm template` and Argo CD, so the chart would render differently from how it installs.
rules.check: Search templates for `lookup` calls whose result feeds rendered resource content.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't render or modify objects the cluster operator owns, such as a shared Gateway (including its backend client certificate) or resources in another component's namespace like a trust-manager `Bundle`. Document the operator's step instead.
rules.why: Such objects serve other workloads and belong to the operator, so a chart that sets them writes into objects it doesn't own.
rules.check: Look for templates that render a `Gateway`, set `spec.tls.backend.clientCertificateRef`, render a trust-manager `Bundle`, or target a namespace other than the release namespace.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't render deprecated Traefik fields such as `ServersTransport` `rootCAsSecrets`. Use `rootCAs` and `certificatesSecrets` instead.

In a Helm chart, a hook Job that writes cluster objects should use the official `kubectl` image pinned by digest. It should not use a shell or a third-party image, and should run `kubectl apply` (for example `apply -k` over a projected volume) instead of deleting and recreating the object.
rules.why: The official image has no shell, and a third-party image widens the supply chain. Delete-and-recreate leaves dependents without the object for a moment on every upgrade.
rules.check: Check hook Job images for a digest pin and a non-official or shell-based image, and check the commands for `sh -c`, `kubectl delete` followed by create, or similar.

rules.statement: When a Helm hook Job mounts a Secret to publish part of it, project only the keys it needs (for example only `ca.crt`), never the whole Secret including its private key.
rules.why: The publisher needs only the CA certificate, and mounting the key would expose it needlessly.
rules.check: Look at the hook Job's projected or secret volume and confirm it uses `items` to select only the public keys.
